calamity_caller.name: Calamity Caller
description: ## Calamity Caller
‹SOURCE Heroes from the Fringe/12›

While all elves feel a deep connection to nature, some elven priests take this bond further, using their link to call down the wrath of nature upon their enemies. Ekujae are most inclined to harness this connection, but any elf can wield their bond to nature in this way.
::prereq{r=Elf}

::ab[Catastrophic Blessing]{icon=info ability="A calamity caller must select a disaster blessing (‹blessing/Earthquake›, ‹blessing/Flood›, ‹blessing/Tornado›, or ‹blessing/Wildfire›) as one of his two blessings, even if the calamity caller's deity does not grant the disaster blessing's associated domain." alter=Blessings}

::ab[Calamity (Su)]{head icon=power standard="A calamity caller can cause a 5-foot square within 30 feet to suffer a calamity. A calamity deals 1d6 damage to creatures within that square. The type of calamity determines what type of damage the calamity deals (see below). An affected creature can attempt a saving throw to reduce this damage by half (DC = 10 + half the calamity caller's warpriest level + the calamity caller's Wisdom modifier); the type of save is determined by the calamity. The calamity caller can use this ability at will." imp4="A calamity caller can create an enhanced calamity when he uses this ability. An enhanced calamity deals twice the calamity's normal damage; in addition, a creature that fails its save suffers an additional effect (see below). A creature must take damage from the calamity to suffer these additional effects. The calamity caller can create an *enhanced calamity* once per day for every 2 warpriest levels he has." imp8="Effects created by an *enhanced calamity* that last for 1 or more rounds persist for 1 additional round." imp12="Enhanced effects now persist for 2 additional rounds." imp16="Enhanced effects now persist for 3 additional rounds." special="The calamities available to calamity callers, the type of damage they deal, the saving throw to resist the damage, and the secondary effect they cause when enhanced, are listed below." replace="Focus weapon~sacred weapon~bonus feats" incrementPlain="The amount of damage~1~2" incrementEnd="d6."}

::ab[Acid Rain]{next icon=ranged ability="A brief rain shower deals acid damage to the target square, with a Fortitude save for half damage. A creature that fails its save against *enhanced* acid rain continues to dissolve for 1 round, automatically taking half the original damage."}

::ab[Blizzard]{next icon=ranged ability="Hail deals cold damage to the target square, with a Fortitude save for half damage. A creature that fails its save against an *enhanced* blizzard is ‹misc/blinded› for 1 round."}

::ab[Deadfall]{next icon=ranged ability="A tree branch, stone boulder, or other heavy object falls on the target square. A deadfall deals bludgeoning damage, with a Reflex save for half damage. A creature that fails its save against an *enhanced* deadfall is knocked ‹rule/prone›." imp12="The target is also ‹misc/confused› for 1 round."}

::ab[Flash Flood]{next icon=ranged ability="A brief surge of stormy water deals bludgeoning damage to the target square, with a Reflex save for half damage. An *enhanced* flash flood does not cause additional effects; instead, an *enhanced* flash flood targets creatures in a 5-foot radius." imp12="The area increases to a 10-foot radius." imp16="The area increases to a 15-foot radius."}

::ab[Lightning Strike]{next icon=ranged ability="A bolt of lightning deals electricity damage to the target square, with a Reflex save for half damage. A creature that fails its save against an *enhanced* lightning strike is ‹misc/staggered› for 1 round by electrical impulses."}

::ab[Thorny Vines]{next icon=ranged ability="Vines covered with thick thorns wrap around the target square. The thorny vines deal piercing damage, with a Reflex save for half damage. A creature that fails its save against *enhanced* thorny vines is ‹rule/entangled› for 1 round."}

::ab[Volcanic Rift]{next icon=ranged ability="A magmatic rift emits a plume of fire into the air, dealing fire damage to the target square, with a Fortitude save for half damage. An *enhanced* volcanic rift also emits poisonous and corrosive gases; a creature that fails its save against the *enhanced* volcanic rift is ‹misc/sickened› for 1 round."}

::ab[Aspect of Disaster (Su)]{l=20 icon=lower passive="A creature affected by a calamity caller's *enhanced calamity* does not receive a save to reduce the damage or avoid the calamity's effects." replace="Aspect of war"}

champion_of_the_faith.name: Champion of the Faith
description: ## Champion of the Faith
‹SOURCE Advanced Class Guide/128›
Champions of the faith are crusaders who use the power of their divine patron to annihilate the faith's enemies.

::ab[Chosen Alignment]{l=1 icon=info choice="A champion of the faith must select one of the following as his chosen alignment: chaos, evil, good, or law. This choice must be one of the alignments shared by the champion of the faith and his deity. Champions of the faith who are neutral with no other alignment components (or whose deity is) can choose any of the above alignments for this purpose. Additionally, a champion of the faith must select the blessing corresponding to his chosen alignment, even if it's not on his deity's list of domains.~~~His chosen alignment's opposite is referred to as his opposed alignment. Good and evil oppose one another, just as law and chaos oppose one another."}

::ab[Sacred Weapon (Su)]{l=1 icon=down-boost info="A champion of the faith gains the *sacred weapon* class feature as normal. However, this ability does not grant the 4th-level ability to enhance the champion of the faith's weapon with divine power, nor does it grant any subsequent increases to that ability." imp4="Any *sacred weapon* wielded by a champion of the faith counts as having his chosen alignment for the purposes of overcoming damage reduction." imp12="Once per day as a @HLswift_action, a champion of the faith can enhance any one *sacred weapon* with a weapon special ability based on his chosen alignment (‹magic-enh/anarchic› for chaos, ‹magic-enh/unholy› for evil, ‹magic-enh/holy› for good, and ‹magic-enh/axiomatic› for law). This effect lasts for 1 minute." imp16="He can use this ability twice a day." imp20="He can use this three times a day." alter="Sacred weapon"}

::ab[Detect Alignment (Sp)]{l=3 icon=magic flavor="A champion of the faith can detect his opposed alignment." move="The champion of the faith can focus on a single item or creature within 60 feet and determine whether it possesses his opposed alignment, as ‹spell/detect «chaos/»evil«/good/law›, learning the strength of the aura as if he had studied it for 3 rounds. The champion of the faith does not detect alignment in any other object or creature when using this ability in this way." replace="Bonus feat gained at 3rd level"}

::ab[Smite (Su)]{l=4 icon=lower-def flavor="A champion of the faith can focus his powers against his chosen foes." swift="The champion of the faith chooses one target within sight to *smite.* If this target is of his opposed alignment, the champion of the faith adds his Charisma bonus (if any) to his attack rolls and adds his warpriest level to all damage rolls made against the target of his *smite.* If the target of his *smite* is an ‹type/outsider› with the subtype corresponding to his opposed alignment, the bonus to damage on the first successful attack increases to 2 points of damage per warpriest level the champion of the faith possesses. Regardless of the target, *smite* attacks automatically bypass any DR the target possesses.~~~In addition, while *smite* is in effect, the champion of the faith gains a deflection bonus equal to his Charisma modifier (if any) to his AC against attacks made by the target of the *smite.* If the *smite* targets a creature that's not of the champion of the faith's opposed alignment, the *smite* is wasted with no effect.~~~The *smite* effect remains until the target of the *smite* is dead or the next time the champion of the faith regains spells." useInc=warpriest~4 useF="4~1~4" special="Using this ability consumes two uses of his *fervor* ability." replace="Channel energy"}

cult_leader.name: Cult Leader
description: ## Cult Leader
‹SOURCE Advanced Class Guide/128›

Referred to as fanatics, lunatics, or obsessives, cultists see themselves as genuine devotees of their deity. And the hierarchs of those devotees, the cult leaders, are the most fanatical of them all. Cult leaders are known for turning reasonable hearts toward corrupted teachings and striking at those that get in the way of their agenda.
::cskill{gain=acro~bluff~dis~ea~kl~per~soh~stl lose=ha~ke~ride~sur~swim}
::ab[Skill Ranks per Level]{icon=boost info="4 + Int modifier."}

::ab[Weapon and Armor Proficiency]{icon=down info="Cult leaders are proficient with all simple weapons, plus the ‹eq-weapon/hand crossbow›, ‹eq-weapon/rapier›, ‹eq-weapon/sap›, ‹eq-weapon/shortbow›, and ‹eq-weapon/short sword›, as well as the favored weapon of their deity. They are proficient with light armor and light shields. The cult leader does not gain ‹feat/Weapon Focus› as a bonus feat as a warpriest normally would." replace="Weapon and armor proficiencies"}
::ab[Well-Hidden (Ex)]{icon=boost passive="A cult leader gains a +2 bonus on Disguise and Stealth checks." replace="Focus weapon"}

::ab[Sneak Attack (Ex)]{l=3 icon=power ability="A cult leader gains the ‹ability/sneak attack› ability, as the rogue class feature. If he already has sneak attack from another class, the extra damage from the classes that grant sneak attack stack for the purpose of determining the sneak attack's extra damage dice. This extra damage is 1d6." incrementPlain="The damage~3~3" incrementEnd="d6." replace="Bonus feats gained at 3rd, 9th, and 15th levels"}
::ab[Enthrall (Sp)]{l=4 icon=magic ability="A cult leader can cast ‹spell/enthrall›. Using this ability consumes two uses of his *fervor* ability." replace="Channel energy"}

::ab[Hide in Plain Sight (Su)]{l=12 icon=power ability="A cult leader can use the Stealth skill even while being observed. As long as he is within 10 feet of an area of ‹rule/dim light›, a cult leader can hide himself from view in the open without anything to actually hide behind. He cannot, however, hide in his own shadow." replace="Bonus feat gained at 12th level"}

disenchanter.name: Disenchanter
description: ## Disenchanter
‹SOURCE Advanced Class Guide/129›

While many warpriests focus on threats to the body, the disenchanter focuses on dangers to the mind and the soul. Using the power of his patron, the disenchanter seeks to keep the powers of magic in check.

::ab[Bonus Feats (Ex)]{icon=info info="Whenever a disenchanter gains a bonus feat, he must choose from the following list: ‹feat/Great Fortitude›, ‹feat/Improved Counterspell›, ‹feat/Iron Will›, ‹feat/Lightning Reflexes›, ‹feat/Skill Focus› (Spellcraft), or ‹feat/Spell Focus› (abjuration)." imp6="He adds the following feats to this list: ‹feat/Dispel Synergy›, ‹feat/Improved Great Fortitude›, ‹feat/Improved Iron Will›, and ‹feat/Improved Lightning Reflexes›." imp12="He adds the following feats to this list: ‹feat/Destructive Dispel›, ‹feat/Dispelling Critical›, ‹feat/Parry Spell›, and ‹feat/Ray Shield›." special="He need not meet the prerequisites for these feats." alter="Bonus feats"}

::ab[Mystic Interference (Su)]{l=4 icon=def-protect ability="A disenchanter can channel a ‹misc/burst› of pure abjuration magic to grant protection to himself and all allies with 30 feet. Affected creatures receive a bonus on saving throws against spells and spell-like abilities for a number of rounds equal to his warpriest level. The bonus is equal to ‹misc/one-fourth› of his warpriest level. This is a sacred bonus if the warpriest is good-aligned or able to spontaneously cast *cure* spells, and a profane bonus if the warpriest is evil-aligned or able to spontaneously cast *inflict* spells. Using this ability consumes two uses of his *fervor* ability." replace="Channel energy"}

::ab[Banish Enchantment (Su)]{l=6 icon=magic flavor="A disenchanter learns to focus his mystic interference." standard="He can consume two uses of his *fervor* ability to target a single creature within 30 feet with a targeted ‹spell/dispel magic›." replace="Bonus feat gained at 6th level"}

divine_champion.name: Divine Champion
description: ## Divine Champion
‹SOURCE Divine Anthology/14›

Divine champions are unswervingly devoted to their causes, and specialize in bringing battle to the enemies of their faiths. They are similar to ‹arc-cleric/divine paragon«s› in many ways, but tend to focus more on their deity's combat prowess rather than seeking to become a physical manifestation of the deity's will.
::ab[Devotion]{icon=info info="A divine champion's power comes from his close connection to his deity. He must worship a deity, and must maintain the same alignment as that deity."}

::ab[Obedient Champion]{l=3 icon=power ability="The divine champion gains ‹feat/Deific Obedience› as a bonus feat, even if he doesn't meet the feat's prerequisites. When a divine champion gains boons from this feat, he gains the appropriate **sentinel** boon offered by his deity, rather than gaining the **exalted** boon." replace="Bonus feat gained at 3rd level"}

::ab[Know the Infidel (Ex)]{l=6 icon=boost flavor="The divine champion becomes an expert at combating enemies of his faith." choice="He must choose a deity whose alignment is opposed to his own deity's alignment in at least one way (good versus evil or law versus chaos); preferably, he should choose a ‹main/faiths>deity whose» alignment<s› diametrically opposes that of his own deity. If the divine champion worships a deity whose alignment is neutral, he must instead select a deity whose alignment is chaotic evil, chaotic good, lawful evil, or lawful good.~~~The choice of this enemy deity is subject to GM approval. At the GM's discretion, the divine champion may be allowed to choose a philosophy or religious organization that's not affiliated with a deity, such as the ‹faith/Green Faith›, the ‹trait/Pure Legion<_recruit›, or the ‹rule/Whispering Way›, but only if that philosophy or religious organization is an enemy of the divine champion's deity." order=ca ability="The divine champion gains a +2 bonus on Bluff, Intimidate, Knowledge, Perception, and Sense Motive checks against followers of the enemy faith, as well as a +2 bonus on weapon attack and damage rolls made against them. Additionally, he can attempt Knowledge skill checks relating to the deity and its church untrained, even if the DC is higher than 10." repeat="The divine champion can select an additional deity to oppose. In addition, the bonus against the followers of any one deity he selected previously (including the one just selected, if so desired) increases by +2.~12~6" replace="Bonus feats gained at 6th, 12th, and 18th levels"}

::ab[Fervent Boon (Sp)]{l=9 icon=magic flavor="A divine champion can call upon his deity for minor boons." ability="By spending *fervor,* he can cast one of the spell-like abilities included in his deity's first **sentinel** boon.~~~By expending one use of *fervor,* he can cast the spell-like ability that the boon normally grants three uses of per day; by expending two uses of *fervor* he can cast the spell-like ability that the boon normally grants twice per day; and by expending three uses of *fervor,* he can cast the spell-like ability that the boon normally grants once per day. These uses don't count against any uses granted by the boon." replace="Bonus feat gained at 9th level"}

divine_commander.name: Divine Commander
description: ## Divine Commander
‹SOURCE Advanced Class Guide/129›

Some warpriests are called to lead great armies and face legions of foes. These divine commanders live for war and fight for glory. Their hearts quicken at battle cries, and they charge forth with their deity's symbol held high. These leaders of armies do so to promote the agenda of their faith, and lead armies of devoted followers willing to give their lives for the cause. (Several of the divine commander's abilities reference and interact with the ‹rule/mass combat« rules›.)

::ab[Mount (Ex)]{icon=power ability="A divine commander gains the service of a loyal and trusty steed to carry her into battle. This mount functions as a druid's ‹sidekick/animal companion›, using the divine commander's level as her effective druid level. The creature must be one that she is capable of riding and must be suitable as a mount.~~~A Medium divine commander can select a ‹companion/camel› or a ‹companion/horse›. A Small divine commander can select a ‹companion/pony› or ‹companion/wolf›, but can also select a ‹companion/boar› or a ‹companion/dog› if she is at least 4th level. (The GM might approve other animals as suitable mounts.)~~~A divine commander does not take an armor check penalty on Ride checks while riding this mount. The mount is always considered combat trained, and begins play with ‹feat/Light Armor Proficiency› as a bonus feat. A divine commander's mount does not gain the *share spells* special ability. Should a divine commander's mount die, she can find another mount to serve her after 1 week of mourning. This new mount does not gain the *link, evasion, devotion,* or *improved evasion* special abilities until the next time the divine commander gains a level." replace=Blessings}

::ab[Battle Tactician (Ex)]{l=3 icon=power order=asu ability="A divine commander gains a ‹main/teamwork feat› as a bonus feat. She must meet the prerequisites for this feat." standard="The divine commander can grant this feat to all allies within 30 feet who can see and hear her. Allies retain the use of this bonus feat for 4 rounds. Allies do not need to meet the prerequisites of this bonus feat." useInc=warpriest~6~3 useF="3~1~6" incrementPlain="The amount of time allies gain this feat~3~2~5~1" incrementEnd=" rounds." replace="Bonus feat gained at 3rd level"}

::ab[Blessed Mount (Su)]{l=6 icon=boost-def ability="A divine commander's mount becomes a creature blessed by his deity. The divine commander's mount gains either the ‹template/celestial›, ‹template/entropic›, ‹template/fiendish›, or ‹template/resolute› template, matching the alignment of the warpriest's deity (celestial for good, entropic for chaotic, fiendish for evil, and resolute for lawful). If the deity matches more than one alignment, the divine commander can select which of the two templates the mount receives. Once the type of template is selected, it cannot be changed.~~~If the divine commander's deity is neutral with no other alignment components, the mount receives spell resistance equal to the divine commander's level + 5, as well as resistance 10 against two types of energy damage of the divine commander's choice.~~~If a divine commander's mount dies and the divine commander finds another mount, the new mount becomes a *blessed mount* the next time the divine commander gains a level." replace="Bonus feat gained at 6th level"}

::ab[Greater Battle Tactician (Ex)]{l=12 icon=power ability="The divine commander gains an additional teamwork feat as a bonus feat. She must meet the prerequisites for this feat. The divine commander can grant this feat to her allies using the *battle tactician* ability.~~~Additionally, using the *battle tactician* ability is now a @HLswift_action." replace="Bonus feat gained at 12th level"}

::ab[Bless Army (Su)]{l=15 icon=boost-protect ability="A divine commander can raise her holy symbol high and give a blessing to the army she is leading. The divine commander's army gains a +1 bonus to the army's ‹rule/OM and DV›. This is a sacred bonus if the warpriest is good-aligned or able to spontaneously cast *cure* spells, and it is a profane bonus if the warpriest is evil-aligned or able to spontaneously cast *inflict* spells." special="Using this ability requires the divine commander to expend two uses of her *fervor* ability. This bonus lasts for 1 battle, and it must be performed during the *tactics* phase of the battle. If this is performed when a mass combat is not imminent, the fervor is spent without granting any bonus." replace="Bonus feat gained at 15th level"}

feral_champion.name: Feral Champion
description: ## Feral Champion
‹SOURCE Ultimate Wilderness/97›
When a warpriest devotes himself to a god of the natural world, he is sometimes blessed with supernatural powers that allow him to evoke animalistic power and fury.
::ab[Feral Blessing]{icon=down info="A feral champion must take the ‹blessing/Animal› blessing and does not gain a second blessing." alter=Blessings}

::ab[Sacred Claws (Su)]{icon=melee ability="Rather than empowering a physical weapon, a feral champion grows claws as primary ‹umr/natural weapons› on each hand. These claws deal damage as a warpriest's *sacred weapon* and can be enhanced as such." alter="Sacred weapon"}

::ab[Wild Shape (Su)]{l=7 icon=power head ability="A feral champion gains *wild shape,* as the ‹class/druid› ability of the same name, and treats his warpriest level - 3 as his effective druid level for the purposes of this ability. However, a feral champion does not gain the ability to take on elemental or plant forms with wild shape." useInc=warpriest~4~7 useF="7~1~4" replace="Sacred armor"}

::ab[Wild Shape (Su)]{next flavor="Text from the druid class ability." icon=power provokes=No standard="You gain the ability to turn yourself into any Small or Medium animal and back again. Your options for new forms include all creatures with the ‹main/monsters_>animal<s› type. This ability functions like the ‹spell/beast shape I› spell, except as noted here. The effect lasts for 1 hour per druid level, or until you change back. The form chosen must be that of an animal with which you are familiar." special="You lose your ability to speak while in animal form because you are limited to the sounds that a normal, untrained animal can make, but you can communicate normally with other animals of the same general grouping as your new form. (The normal sound a wild parrot makes is a squawk, so changing to this form does not permit speech.)" imp6="You can *wild shape* as ‹spell/beast shape II›, and you can now change into a Large or Tiny animal." imp8="You can *wild shape* as ‹spell/beast shape III›, and you can now change into a Huge or Diminutive animal."}

fist_of_the_godclaw.name: Fist of the Godclaw
description: ## Fist of the Godclaw
‹SOURCE Disciple's Doctrine/12›
Devoted to the divine control of law above all else, these zealots seek to establish absolute order. Disciplined and precise, they lead their allies against the chaotic hordes.
::prereq{other="Must be of a lawful alignment (in addition to the normal alignment restrictions)."}

::ab[Deity]{icon=info info="A fist of the Godclaw must worship ‹faith/Abadar›, ‹faith/Asmodeus›, ‹faith/Iomedae›, ‹faith/Irori›, or ‹faith/Torag›. Alternatively, the fist of the Godclaw must venerate the pantheon of these deities known as the Godclaw."}
::ab[Blessings of the Godclaw (Ex)]{icon=down info="A fist of the Godclaw must select the ‹blessing/Law› blessing and the ‹blessing/Godclaw› blessing." alter=Blessings}

::ab[Detect Chaos (Sp)]{l=3 icon=magic ability="A fist of the Godclaw can cast ‹spell/detect chaos› three times per day as a spell-like ability, using his warpriest level as his caster level. If the fist of the Godclaw already has, or later gains, the ability to cast *detect chaos,* then he can cast *detect chaos* at will as a spell-like ability." replace="Bonus feat gained at 3rd level"}

::ab[Alignment Channel (Su)]{l=6 icon=power ability="A fist of the Godclaw gains ‹feat/Alignment Channel› as a bonus feat. When he uses this feat and spends *fervor* to *channel energy,* he can harm only outsiders with the chaotic subtype. Additionally, when using this feat, he expends only one use of his *fervor* to *channel energy* and deals 1d6 points of damage for every 2 warpriest levels he has." imp12="A fist of the Godclaw can expend an additional use of *fervor* to *channel energy* as a @HLmove_action." replace="Bonus feats gained at 6th level and 12th level"}

::ab[Aspect of Law (Ex)]{l=20 icon=boost-def-roll flavor="A fist of the Godclaw can channel an aspect of law, growing even more inflexible." swift="Once per day, a warpriest can treat his level as his base attack bonus, gains DR 20/chaotic, and becomes immune to mind-affecting effects. In addition, he can take the average result on any die roll instead of rolling normally. This ability lasts for 1 minute." replace="Aspect of war"}

forgepriest.name: Forgepriest
description: ## Forgepriest
‹SOURCE Advanced Class Guide/130›
Armorers of exquisite skill, forgepriests take inspiration from their deity to produce the most perfect weapons and armor they can, the better to equip the armies of the faithful.
::ab[Blessings]{icon=down info="A forgepriest selects only one blessing." alter=Blessings}

::ab[Smith's Spells]{icon=learn info="A forgepriest adds the following spells to his spell list at the listed spell level." s1="Jury rig~shield" s2="Heat metal~shatter" s3="Keen edge~quench~versatile weapon" s4="Wreath of blades" s5="Fabricate~major creation" s6="Mage's sword›"}

::ab[Forge Mastery (Ex)]{l=2 icon=boost passive="A forgepriest adds a bonus equal to half his level to all Craft checks to make metal items, armor, and weapons." replace="2nd blessing normally gained by a warpriest"}
::ab[Bonus Feats]{icon=boost info="A forgepriest can select ‹main/item creation feat«s› in addition to combat feats when he gains a bonus feat." alter="Bonus feats"}
::ab[Craft Magic Arms and Armor]{l=3 icon=power ability="A forgepriest gains ‹feat/Craft Magic Arms and Armor› as a bonus feat." replace="Bonus feat gained at 3rd level"}

::ab[Creator's Bond (Su)]{l=4 icon=boost ability="When a forgepriest uses his *sacred weapon* ability with an item he created personally, he can expend two uses of his *fervor* ability to increase the bonus granted by 1." special="Once the forgepriest has the *sacred armor* ability, he can also use this ability in conjunction with that." replace="Channel energy"}
::ab[Heat of the Forge (Su)]{icon=def l6="A forgepriest gains fire resistance 5." l13="This resistance increases to 10." replace="Bonus feat gained at 6th level"}

jistkan_magistrate.name: Jistkan Magistrate
description: ## Jistkan Magistrate
‹SOURCE Blood of the Ancients/17›

Some warpriests study the ancient magic that the Jistkan magistrates used to bind elementals and make pacts with genies. By tapping into the elementals' primal magic, these warpriests gain powers that help them in combat.
::prereq{other="Must worship a deity who grants the ‹blessing/Air›, ‹blessing/Earth›, ‹blessing/Fire›, or ‹blessing/Water› blessing"}
::cskill{gain=kp lose=sur}
::ab[Elemental Binder (Su)]{icon=down info="A Jistkan magistrate must select the Air, Earth, Fire, or Water blessing. He does not gain a second blessing." alter=Blessings}

::ab[Spontaneous Summons]{flavor="A Jistkan magistrate is extremely flexible in channeling his stored spell energy." icon=magic ability="In addition to losing prepared spells to cast &quot&cure&quot& or &quot&inflict&quot& spells, he can also lose a prepared spell in order to cast any ‹spell/summon monster› spell of the same level or lower. He can use this ability only to summon an ‹family/elemental› whose subtype matches his blessing. He can expend one use of his *fervor* ability to decrease the spell's casting time to 1 @HLstandard_action and to increase the spell's duration to 1 minute per level." alter="Spontaneous casting"}

::ab[Bonus Languages]{icon=boost passive="A Jistkan magistrate's bonus language options include Aquan, Auran, Ignan, and Terran instead of Abyssal, Celestial, and Infernal. These choices are in addition to the bonus languages available to the character because of his race." alter="Bonus languages"}
:::ab{title="Channel Element (Su)" action=Ability l=4 icon=power alter=Channel}

A Jistkan magistrate gains ‹feat/Elemental Channel› as a bonus feat, choosing the elemental subtype that matches his blessing. He doesn't gain the ability to harm undead with channeled energy (if he channels positive energy) or heal undead (if he channels negative energy). Instead, he can channel a blast of elemental matter and energy that buffets his targets. The Jistkan artificer's blessing determines the damage type of this attack, as indicated by the table below. A successful Reflex save halves the damage.
| Blessing | Damage type |
| Air | Electricity |
| Earth | Acid |
| Fire | Fire |
| Water | Cold |

libertys_blade.name: Liberty's Blade
description: ## Liberty's Blade
‹SOURCE Advanced Class Origins/24›

There are some who find in the call to freedom something primal and spiritual, even more so than other Andorens. These liberty's blades become warpriests of deities who spread freedom, and they head to lives of adventure as ‹rule/Eagle Knights› or adventurers, championing liberty wherever they go.
::prereq{other="Must worship a good deity who grants the Liberation blessing"}
::ab[Freedom's Focus (Su)]{icon=down info="A liberty's blade must select the ‹blessing/Liberation› blessing. He does not gain a second blessing." alter=Blessings}
::ab[Devilslayer (Su)]{l=4 icon=boost ability="A liberty's blade adds ‹magic-enh/devil »bane› to the list of enhancements he can add to his *sacred weapon.*" alter="Sacred weapon"}

mantis_zealot.name: Mantis Zealot
description: ## Mantis Zealot
‹SOURCE Adventurer's Guide/157;Advanced Class Origins/25›

Among the ‹rule/Red Mantis› worshipers of Achaekek, some hold such strong faith in their assassin god that they gain divine power. They forge themselves into perfect killers in honor of He Who Walks in Blood. These warpriests are a relatively recent addition to the Red Mantis arsenal, but in the few short decades they have served the assassins, they have quickly built a reputation for themselves as particularly fanatical devotees of the Mantis God. Their penchant for taking the faith's writings verbatim and for overwhelming and often destructive pedantry serves them well in matters of loyalty to Achaekek (and particularly when it comes to drafting contracts for assassinations that favor the organization in financial and tactical ways), but it offers little room for complex cases that would benefit from bending the rules, making them unsuitable for missions that require diplomatic finesse. In addition, the rising incidence of mantis zealots accusing fellow worshipers of Achaekek of heresy and blasphemy, resulting in internal accusations, exiles, and even fullblown assassinations, increasingly makes them objects of fear and distrust among even their own kind. Whether the rise of the mantis zealot presages a dramatic upcoming shift in the religion's hierarchy and methods, or whether the faction may be burning too bright for its own good and is hurtling toward self-annihilation, remains to be seen.

::ab[Mantis Sworn (Ex)]{icon=warning info="A mantis zealot must choose ‹faith/Achaekek› as his deity, and he must be lawful evil in alignment. If he ever changes his deity, he loses this archetype and becomes a normal warpriest."}

::ab[Weapon and Armor Proficiency]{icon=down ability="Mantis zealots are proficient with simple and martial weapons, as well as with the ‹eq-weapon/sawtooth sabre›. They are proficient with light armor but not with shields." replace="Weapon and armor proficiencies"}

This ability functions as the rogue class feature of the same name, and his sneak attack damage is +1d6." increment="This damage~4~4" incrementEnd="d6." special="If the zealot gets a sneak attack bonus from another source, the bonuses stack." replace="Sacred weapon"}

If he already has the uncanny dodge ability from another source, he instead gains ‹ability/improved uncanny dodge› while this ability is active." useL=warpriest useUnit=minute useNC=1 imp10="When he uses this ability, he also gains ‹ability/evasion› as per the ‹class/monk› class feature (or ‹ability/improved evasion› if he already has evasion from another source)." imp13="He gains *improved uncanny dodge* instead of *uncanny dodge.*" imp16="He can activate this ability as part of making an initiative check, before rolling the die." imp19="He gains *improved evasion* instead of *evasion.*" replace="Sacred armor"}

::ab[Aspect of the Mantis (Su)]{l=20 icon=boost ability="When using *aspect of war,* instead of moving at full speed regardless of his armor or encumbrance, a mantis zealot deals a number of points of ‹rule/bleed› damage equal to his Dexterity modifier with each attack." alter="Aspect of war"}

molthuni_arsenal_chaplain.name: Molthuni Arsenal Chaplain
description: ## Molthuni Arsenal Chaplain
‹SOURCE Weapon Master's Handbook/6›
Molthuni arsenal chaplains are warpriests trained in the Arsenal District in Korholm. They bolster their nation's military by focusing on the militant aspects of their gods.

::ab[War Blessing (Su)]{icon=power-down ability="A Molthuni arsenal chaplain must choose ‹blessing/War› as his blessing, and can do so even if it is a domain not normally granted by his deity. He does not receive a second blessing." imp7="A Molthuni arsenal chaplain gains ‹feat/Quicken Blessing› (War) as a bonus feat even if he does not meet the prerequisites, but cannot grant a War blessing to himself as a swift action with Quicken Blessing until he is at least 10th level." imp13="A Molthuni arsenal chaplain can use the War blessing on an ally at a range of up to 30 feet by spending an additional use of the blessing ability." imp16="A Molthuni arsenal chaplain can use the War blessing on a second target with a single use of the blessing ability." imp19="A Molthuni arsenal chaplain can use the War blessing on any number of targets at once with a single use of the blessing ability." alter=Blessing replace="Sacred armor"}

This bonus also applies to your ‹rule/CMD› when defending against ‹rule/disarm› and ‹rule/sunder› attempts made against weapons from this group." imp9="You select a new weapon group and gain the +1 bonus when using weapons from that group. proclaimer.name: Proclaimer
description: ## Proclaimer
‹SOURCE People of the Wastes/19›

A proclaimer is the polar opposite of a ‹arc-paladin/faithful wanderer« (paladin)›, rushing into Abyss-twisted wastes with nothing but his weapon in his hand and his faith in his heart, shouting his deity's name to the skies. Most proclaimers don't survive their first day in a hostile environment, but those who do become the stuff of legend, bolstering the spirits of crusaders near and far.
::ab[Righteous Oath]{icon=info info="A proclaimer cannot be evil or worship an evil deity, and he must choose ‹main/cure spells› for his spontaneous casting." alter=Spellcasting}

::ab[Cleanser of Evil (Su)]{l=2 icon=aura-down swift="A proclaimer can hold his weapon aloft and shout his deity's name, spending one use of *fervor* to deal 1d6 points of damage to all evil outsiders within 5 feet. This damage has the same alignment as the proclaimer's deity (for example, it counts as good and lawful for a worshiper of ‹faith/Ragathiel› who uses this ability)." imp7="The effect expands to include an area within 10 feet of the proclaimer." imp13="The effect expands to 15 feet." imp19="The effect expands to 20 feet." special="A proclaimer can't use *fervor* to damage undead or to heal." incrementPlain="This damage~2~3" incrementEnd="d6." alter=Fervor replace="Sacred armor"}

::ab[Zone of Sanctification (Su)]{l=4 icon=aura ability="When a proclaimer uses *fervor* to damage evil outsiders with his *cleanser of evil* ability, he can spend one additional use of *fervor* as a @HLmove_action to create a *zone of sanctification* in the same area for 1 round. All evil outsiders in the *zone* when it becomes active must succeed at a Will saving throw (DC 10 + half the proclaimer's level + his Wisdom modifier) or be pushed back until they are out of the area. Evil outsiders that end their turns in the area take damage as if affected by *cleanser of evil.*" replace="Channel energy"}

proselytizer.name: Proselytizer
description: ## Proselytizer
‹SOURCE Cohorts and Companions/24›

The proselytizer is the perfect militant missionary. He seeks to win the hearts and lay claim to the souls of those he meets, and - failing that - spreads the word of his deity at the edge of the sword.

::ab[Weapon and Armor Proficiencies]{icon=down-power info="A proselytizer does not gain proficiency with heavy armor or with all martial weapons, though he does gain proficiency in his deity's favored weapon. If his deity's favored weapon is unarmed strike, he gains ‹feat/Improved Unarmed Strike› as a bonus feat." alter="Weapon and armor proficiencies"}

::ab[Emotional Appeal]{flavor="A proselytizer has great power over the emotions of others, wielding his voice like a weapon to pierce the heart of listeners and bring them closer to communion with his deity's power." icon=learn info="The warpriest adds the following spells to his warpriest spell list at the indicated spell levels. He casts these as divine warpriest spells." s1="Charm person~rally point~wrath" s2=Castigate~heroism~suggestion s3="Charm monster~lesser geas" s4="Forced repentance~serenity" s5="Mass castigate~mass suggestion" s6=Antipathy~sympathy replace="Sacred armor~3rd-level bonus feat"}

::ab[Sacred Subdual (Su)]{icon=down ability="When a proselytizer uses his *sacred weapon* damage in place of his normal weapon damage, all damage he deals with that weapon is nonlethal damage." alter="Sacred weapon"}

::ab[Blessing of Conversion]{icon=info-down info="The proselytizer always gains the conversion bonus (see below) upon converting an NPC, rather than only the first time he does so each level. The bonuses overlap their durations, and do not stack." imp3="The proselytizer does not gain access to the minor blessings granted by his *blessing* class feature until 3rd level." alter=Blessings}

::ab[Voice of the Faithful (Ex)]{icon=power l10="A proselytizer of can expend a use of his major blessing to be able to speak to and understand any creature with a language for 1 hour." alter="Blessings (major)"}
::h3[Converting NPCs]{jl}

Cohorts and their masters often share alignment, but a common religion can be just as important. A cohort may share a leader's faith when first recruited, or a PC may seek to convert a cohort as their relationship develops.

While PCs may choose to change alignment, such changes for NPCs may require magical assistance (see the ‹spell/atonement› spell). Alternatively, you can proselytize for your patron deity, using your powers of persuasion and social influence to indoctrinate an NPC in the dogma of the faith while inspiring their fealty.

Converting an NPC to your faith is similar to modifying their reaction with Diplomacy. You can only attempt to convert NPCs who are at least indifferent toward you, though you can take time to make a hostile or unfriendly NPC indifferent, and then begin the process of conversion. The DC of a conversion depends on how many conversion steps away from your faith an NPC is, starting at one conversion step for an NPC with no significant faith who matches your faith's alignment. For each step the NPC's alignment differs from the alignment of your faith, add one conversion step. If the NPC already holds a significant religious belief, add an additional conversion step. Note that servants of other faiths - including divine spellcasters who worship a deity and agents in the employ of a formal religion - normally can never be converted to a new faith. The GM has final discretion over whether an NPC will ever convert to your beliefs.

If the GM rules that an NPC can be converted, the DC to convert that NPC is 10 + the NPC's Hit Dice + the NPC's Wisdom or Charisma modifier (whichever is higher) + 5 per conversion step. For example, a 5th level warrior with a Wisdom of 12 and no existing significant faith and who is the same alignment as your deity has a conversion DC of 21. Each conversion attempt requires at least an hour of proselytizing, and you can attempt no more than one conversion check per week. For your conversion attempt, roll a Diplomacy check and a Knowledge (religion) check at the DC determined above. If you succeed at both checks, decrease the number of conversion steps for that NPC by one. If you fail either check, you reinforce the NPC's existing faith and add one to the number of conversion steps for that NPC. If you fail three checks over the course of a conversion effort, the NPC rejects your faith and you cannot attempt another conversion for a year. However, if the number of conversion steps ever reaches 0, you convince the NPC to adopt your religion. Note that this does not necessarily change the NPC's alignment, so you could manage to convince a chaotic evil harpy to worship her own very odd form of Shelyn.

While proselytizing is a reasonable activity for a religious adventurer, it should be handled with sensitivity, both in character and at the gaming table. Having a PC repeatedly attempt to convert NPCs who aren't interested is likely to result in worsening their attitude toward the character, and significant effort may be required to restore those relationships. Some players may be uncomfortable with too much time being spent on religious talk, in which case a GM is free to simply treat the conversion as a skill check, without actually roleplaying the talks that allow the conversion check to take place.
::h3[Successful Conversion]{jl}

Characters that successfully convert others to their faith can gain divine blessings for adding new members to their religion. The first time at each character level a PC converts an NPC, they gain a conversion bonus for a number of days equal to the level of the NPC converted. Typical conversion bonuses for various faiths, and examples of classes likely to be interested in converting, are listed on the following page. In the case of Neutral deities, the bonus may be a sacred or profane bonus as most appropriate for the PC who gains it.

sacred_fist.name: Sacred Fist
description: ## Sacred Fist
‹SOURCE Advanced Class Guide/130›
Unlike many warpriests, sacred fists leave behind armor and shield and instead rely on their fists and whatever protection their deity bestows on them.
::cskill{gain=acro~ea~kh~per~stl lose=ha~ke~sur}

::ab[Weapon and Armor Proficiency]{icon=power-down info="Sacred fists are proficient with the ‹eq-weapon/club›, ‹eq-weapon/light crossbow›, ‹eq-weapon/heavy crossbow›, ‹eq-weapon/dagger›, ‹eq-weapon/handaxe›, ‹eq-weapon/javelin›, ‹eq-weapon/kama›, ‹eq-weapon/nunchaku›, ‹eq-weapon/quarterstaff›, ‹eq-weapon/sai›, ‹eq-weapon/shortspear›, ‹eq-weapon/short sword›, ‹eq-weapon/shuriken›, ‹eq-weapon/siangham›, ‹eq-weapon/sling›, and ‹eq-weapon/spear›. Sacred fists are not proficient with any armor or shields." special="When wearing armor, using a shield, or carrying a medium or heavy load, a sacred fist loses his *AC bonus* and *flurry of blows.*" replace="Weapon and armor proficiency"}

::ab[AC Bonus (Su)]{flavor="A deity protects her sacred fist as long as he is unarmored and unencumbered." icon=def passive="A sacred fist adds his Wisdom modifier (minimum 0) to his AC and his CMD." imp4="A sacred fist gains a dodge bonus to AC and CMD. This bonus is equal to ‹misc/one-fourth› of his warpriest level." special="These bonuses to AC apply even against touch attacks or when the sacred fist is flat-footed. He loses these bonuses when he is immobilized or helpless, when he wears any armor, when he carries a shield, or when he carries a medium or heavy load.~~~This counts as the ‹class/monk› ability of the same name, and the sacred fist's warpriest levels stack with monk levels for determining the benefits."}

::ab[Flurry of Blows (Ex)]{l=1 head icon=melee ability="A sacred fist can make a flurry of blows attack as a full-attack action. This ability works like the monk ability of the same name, except the sacred fist's attack bonus from warpriest levels does not count as his warpriest level." replace="Sacred weapon"}

:::ab{next title="Flurry of Blows (Ex)" flavor="Text from the monk class ability." icon=melee action=Ability imp8="You can make two additional attacks when you use flurry of blows, as if using ‹feat/Improved Two-Weapon Fighting› (even if you do not meet the prerequisites for the feat)." imp15="You can make three additional attacks when you use flurry of blows, as if using ‹feat/Greater Two-Weapon Fighting› (even if you do not meet the prerequisites for the feat)."}

You can make a flurry of blows as a full-attack action. When doing so you may make one additional attack using any combination of unarmed strikes or attacks with a special monk weapon (kama, nunchaku, quarterstaff, sai, shuriken, and siangham) as if using the ‹feat/Two-Weapon Fighting› feat (even if you do not meet the prerequisites for the feat). For the purpose of these attacks, your base attack bonus from your monk class levels is equal to your monk level. For all other purposes, such as qualifying for a feat or a prestige class, you use your normal base attack bonus.

You apply your full Strength bonus to your damage rolls for all successful attacks made with flurry of blows, whether the attacks are made with an off-hand or with a weapon wielded in both hands. You may substitute ‹rule/disarm›, ‹rule/sunder›, and ‹rule/trip› combat maneuvers for unarmed attacks as part of a flurry of blows. You cannot use any weapon other than an unarmed strike or a special monk weapon as part of a flurry of blows. You cannot use natural weapons (if you have any) as part of a flurry of blows, nor can you make natural attacks in addition to your flurry of blows attacks.

::ab[Unarmed Strike]{l=1 head icon=power ability="A sacred fist gains ‹feat/Improved Unarmed Strike› as a bonus feat. He uses his warpriest levels as monk levels for determining the amount of damage dealt with an unarmed strike." replace="Focus weapon"}

::ab[Unarmed Strike]{next flavor="Relevant text from the monk class." icon=melee info="The amount of damage you deal depends on your size." imp1="Your unarmed strike deals 1d4 (Small), 1d6 (Medium), or 1d8 (Large) damage." imp4="Your unarmed strike now deals 1d6 (Small), 1d8 (Medium), or 2d6 (Large) damage." imp8="Your unarmed strike now deals 1d8 (Small), 1d10 (Medium), or 2d8 (Large) damage." imp12="Your unarmed strike now deals 1d10 (Small), 2d6 (Medium), or 3d6 (Large) damage." imp16="Your unarmed strike now deals 2d6 (Small), 2d8 (Medium), or 3d8 (Large) damage." imp20="Your unarmed strike now deals 2d8 (Small), 2d10 (Medium), or 4d8 (Large) damage."}

::ab[Blessed Fortitude (Su)]{l=3 icon=def flavor="A sacred fist can avoid even magical and unusual attacks with help from his deity." passive="If he succeeds at a Fortitude saving throw against an attack that has a reduced effect on a successful save, he instead avoids the effect entirely." special="A ‹misc/helpless› sacred fist does not gain the benefit of the blessed fortitude ability." replace="Bonus feat gained at 3rd level"}

::ab[Bonus Style Feat]{l=6 icon=power ability="The sacred fist gains a ‹main/style feat› as a bonus feat. The sacred fist must meet the style feat's prerequisites. He uses his warpriest levels as monk levels for the purposes of meeting the feat's prerequisites." repeat="A sacred fist gains either another style feat or a feat that requires a style feat as a prerequisite.~12~6" replace="Bonus feats gained at 6th, 12th, and 18th levels"}

::ab[Ki Pool (Su)]{l=7 head icon=power-def order=aw ability="The sacred fist gains a ki pool. This functions as the monk class feature, using the sacred fist's level - 3 as his monk level when determining the number of points in his pool and bonuses granted to his unarmed strike." swift="Additionally, the sacred fist can spend 1 point from his ki pool to grant himself a +1 insight bonus to his AC for 1 minute. (This is in addition the normal ki ability to gain a dodge bonus to AC.) This insight bonus increases by 1 for every 3 levels above 7th (to a maximum of +5 at 19th level)." replace="Sacred armor"}

::ab[Ki Pool (Su)]{next flavor="Text from the monk class ability." icon=magic-melee order=awp ability="You gain a pool of ki points. The number of points in your ki pool is equal to 1/2 your monk level + your Wisdom modifier." passive="As long as you have at least 1 point in your ki pool, you can make a *ki strike,* which allows your unarmed attacks to be treated as magic weapons for the purpose of overcoming ‹rule/damage reduction›." imp7="Your *ki strikes* are also treated as cold iron and silver for the purpose of overcoming damage reduction." imp10="Your *ki strikes* are also treated as lawful weapons for the purpose of overcoming damage reduction." imp16="Your *ki strikes* are treated as ‹eq-material/adamantine› weapons for the purpose of overcoming damage reduction and bypassing ‹rule/hardness›." swift="By spending 1 point from your ki pool, you can make one additional unarmed strike at your highest attack bonus when making a flurry of blows attack. In addition, you can spend 1 point to increase your speed by 20 feet for 1 round. Finally, your can spend 1 point from your *ki* pool to give yourself a +4 dodge bonus to AC for 1 round." special="The ki pool is replenished each morning after 8 hours of rest or meditation; these hours do not need to be consecutive."}

::ab[Miraculous Fortitude (Su)]{l=9 icon=def passive="The sacred fist's *blessed fortitude* ability improves. He still takes no damage or negative effect when he succeeds at a Fortitude save, but now when he fails a Fortitude saving throw against a spell or effect that deals damage (including ‹rule/ability damage« and» drain›), he takes only half the amount of damage." special="A ‹misc/helpless› sacred fist does not gain the benefit of *miraculous fortitude.*" replace="Bonus feat gained at 9th level"}

shieldbearer.name: Shieldbearer
description: ## Shieldbearer
‹SOURCE Armor Master's Handbook/7›

Shieldbearers are divine warriors who stand on the front lines of battle, shoulder to shoulder with the soldiers of their people. The shieldbearer tradition has long been a strong legacy among the dwarves of the Five Kings Mountains, while many young women throughout the Lands of the Linnorm Kings and Realm of the Mammoth Lords become shieldbearers known as shield maidens. Shieldbearers among the Shoanti are often advisors as well as combatants, while in the Mwangi Expanse shieldbearers are known for defending entire villages from the Gorilla King's minions.

::ab[Shield Adept (Ex)]{l=1 icon=power-def ability="A shieldbearer receives ‹feat/Improved Shield Bash› as a bonus feat. When carrying a shield, the shieldbearer adds his shield bonus on ‹rule/concentration› checks to cast defensively." replace="Focus weapon"}

::ab[Sacred Weapon (Su)]{icon=info-down ability="A shieldbearer treats shields as *sacred weapons* (instead of his god's favored weapon), though the shieldbearer can still designate additional weapons as *sacred weapons* by selecting them with the ‹feat/Weapon Focus› feat. The shieldbearer's *sacred weapon* damage applies only to attacks made with shields." imp7="The shieldbearer does not gain the ability to enhance *sacred weapons* until 7th level." increment="The *sacred weapon* bonus~7~3" alter="Sacred weapon~sacred armor"}

::ab[Sacred Shield (Su)]{l=4 icon=def swift="A shieldbearer gains the ability to enhance his shield with divine power. This ability functions as the *sacred armor* ability, except as follows. This power grants the shield an enhancement bonus equal to ‹misc/one-fourth› of his warpriest level (this bonus does not act as an attack or damage bonus when the shield is used in a shield bash)." special="The shieldbearer can enhance a shield with any of the following armor special abilities (instead of those listed for *sacred armor*): ‹magic-enh/arrow deflection›, ‹magic-enh/blinding›, ‹magic-enh/fortification› (heavy, light, or moderate), ‹magic-enh/reflecting›, and ‹magic-enh/spell resistance› (13, 15, 17, and 19)."}
::ab[Channel Energy (Su)]{icon=down-cone info="The shieldbearer can *channel energy* only when carrying a shield, and the ability manifests as a 30-foot-cone ‹misc/burst›, rather than as a radius."}

sixth_wing_bulwark.name: Sixth Wing Bulwark
description: ## Sixth Wing Bulwark
‹SOURCE Distant Realms/32›

Many are the followers of Ragathiel who lead in battle. Far fewer, but no less crucial to a successful campaign, are those who hold the line and defend against the incursion of evil forces. The Sixth Wing bulwark trains to do just that: fortifying herself and her allies to stand strong in the face of any opposition, no matter how dire.

::ab[Sixth Wing Sworn]{icon=warning info="A Sixth Wing bulwark must be a worshiper of ‹faith/Ragathiel›. If she ever changes her deity, she loses this archetype, cannot regain it, and becomes a normal warpriest."}
::ab[Weapon and Armor Proficiency]{icon=power ability="A Sixth Wing bulwark gains proficiency in ‹eq-armor/tower shield«s›." alter="Weapon and armor proficiencies"}
::ab[Focus Shield]{icon=power ability="A Sixth Wing bulwark gains ‹feat/Shield Focus› as a bonus feat." replace="Focus weapon"}

::ab[Sacred Shield (Su)]{icon=boost-def-protect ability="Dedicated training and divine grace allow a Sixth Wing bulwark to lessen the burden of a shield's weight.
